dialogue.content: We are downsizing near Limerick and want our old furniture considered before buying.
Please send each piece’s full dimensions, some photographs and a measured house plan. We can then see what you can keep before choosing anything new.
Here is the house plan. We still need to check its measurements on site.
The rooms shown add up to 81.7 square metres inside. We can use that as a starting point and confirm it when the house is measured.
The biggest generic room is the lounge and the other generic rooms are bedrooms.
That gives you a 20.4 square metre lounge without moving its walls. I will keep the existing doorways and windows in mind as we look at where your furniture could go.
Start with a compact sofa and table; they can stand in for our pieces until measured.
For now, I have allowed for a 2000 millimetre sofa and a 900 by 550 millimetre coffee table. When you send your own pieces’ measurements, we can see how they compare.
The main bed can use 140 and the spare 90, with wardrobes 120 across.
I will allow for the full bed frames and the wardrobes. We can choose the actual products with the designer once we know which existing pieces you want to keep.
Could you also promise new flooring, curtains and a fully wired lighting plan?

Those are broader project requirements that must be scoped with the designer. This calculation contains furniture placement only; it has not measured curtain drops, electrical circuits or flooring quantities.
Keep those questions open and tell us whether the first arrangement fits.
Six pieces fit in the drawing, with one measurement still to check. The visit will help you and the designer settle their final positions.
Fine; we will send the real dimensions before choosing anything final.

I deliver a preliminary furniture study with the retained-piece measurements and wider project scope still pending. The designer has the final decision on what can be reused, specified or made for your home.
